21:78: Ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Marra on the authority of Ibn Masoud: That field was a vineyard with its clusters hanging down, and Shuraih said the same. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Nafsh is grazing. Shuraih, Al-Zuhri and Qatadah said: Al-Nafsh only occurs at night, Qatadah added: And Al-Halal during the day. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb and Harun bin Idris Al-Asamm told us, they said: Al-Maharibi told us on the authority of Ash'ath on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Marra on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, when the sheep of the people had pastured therein, he said: A vineyard whose clusters had grown and spoiled it. He said: So David ruled that the sheep should go to the owner of the vineyard, and Solomon said: Other than this, O Prophet of God. He said: What is that? He said: The vineyard is given to the owner of the sheep, so he takes care of it until it returns to how it was, and the sheep are given to the owner of the vineyard, so he takes some of it until the vineyard is as it was, then the vineyard is given to its owner, and the sheep are given to their owner. That is what he said: So We gave it to Solomon. And Al-Awfi narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Ali bin Zaid: Khalifa told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: David ruled in favor of the owners of the farmland regarding the sheep. The shepherds came out with their dogs, and Solomon said to them: How did he rule between you? They told him, and he said: If I were in charge of your affairs, I would rule differently. David was told about that, so he called him and said: How do you rule between them? He said: I will give the sheep to the owner of the farmland, so he will have their offspring, milk, offal, and benefits, and the owners of the sheep will sow for the people of the farmland the same as their crops. When the crops reach what they were on, the owners of the farms will take them and return the sheep to their owners. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, Khadij told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Masruq, who said: The field in which the people’s sheep grazed was a vineyard in which the sheep grazed and did not leave a leaf or a cluster of grapes without eating it. So they came to David, who gave them their necks, but Sulaiman said: No, rather the sheep will be taken and given to the people of the vineyard, so their milk and benefit will be theirs, and the people of the sheep will be given the vineyard, so they will inhabit it and repair it until it returns to what it was on the night the sheep grazed it. Then the people of the sheep will be given their sheep and the people of the vineyard their vineyard. And this is what Shuraih, Marra, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and others said. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abi Ziyad told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Aamer, who said: Two men came to Shuraih, and one of them said: This sheep of mine cut some of my yarn. Shuraih said: During the day or at night? If it was during the day, then the owner of the sheep was absolved, and if it was at night, then he was liable. Then he recited: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field (al-Ahkam al-Lail 10:14). What Shuraih said is similar to what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Layth bin Sa’d, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Haram bin Muhaysah, that the she-camel of al-Bara’ bin Azib entered a garden and caused damage to it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the people of the garden should protect it during the day, and that whatever the livestock cause at night is liable to its owners. He explained this hadith, and we have discussed it in detail in the Book of Rulings. And God is the Grantor of success. And His statement: And We gave Solomon understanding of it, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad told us on the authority of Hamid that when Iyas bin Muawiyah was appointed a judge, Al-Hasan came to him and cried, so he said: What makes you cry? He said: O Abu Saeed, it has reached me that among judges, a man who strives hard and makes a mistake is in the Fire, a man who is led astray by desire is in the Fire, and a man who strives hard and gets it right is in Paradise. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: In what God narrated of the story of David and Solomon, peace be upon them, and the prophets, there is a ruling that refutes the words of these people about their words. God the Almighty said: “And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field when the sheep of the people had pastured therein. And We were witnesses to their judgment.” So God praised Solomon and did not criticize David. Then he said - meaning Al-Hasan - “God has imposed three conditions on the judges: they should not exchange it for a small price, they should not follow their own desires, and they should not fear anyone in it.” Then he recited: O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow their own desires, for they will lead you astray from the way of God. And He said: So do not fear the people, but fear Me. And He said: And do not exchange My verses for a small price. I said: As for the prophets, peace be upon them, they are all infallible and supported by God the Almighty, and there is no disagreement about this among the established scholars from the predecessors and successors. As for those other than them, it has been proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Amr ibn Al-Aas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the judge exerts his effort and is correct, he will have two rewards, and if he exerts his effort and is wrong, he will have one reward. This hadith explicitly refutes what Iyas imagined, that if the judge exerts his effort and is wrong, he will be in Hell. And God knows best. In the Sunnah: Judges are of three types: one judge in Paradise, and two judges in Hell. A man who knew the truth and judged accordingly is in Paradise, a man who judged between people out of ignorance is in Hell, and a man who knew the truth and judged contrary to it is in Hell. Similar to this story mentioned in the Qur’an is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad where he said: Ali bin Hafs told us, Warqa’ told us on the authority of Abu al-Zinad on the authority of al-A’raj on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “While two women were with their two sons, a wolf came and took one of the sons, so they went to David and he judged in favor of the elder one. They went out and Solomon called them and said: Bring the knife so that I may cut him between you. The younger one said: May God have mercy on you, he is her son, do not cut him. So he judged in favor of the younger one.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs, and al-Nasa’i included it in a chapter in the Book of Judgment: Chapter on the judge who suggests contrary to the ruling in order to learn the truth. And thus the story that Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Solomon, peace be upon him, from his history, through Al-Hasan Ibn Sufyan, on the authority of Safwan Ibn Salih, on the authority of Al-Walid Ibn Muslim, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Bashir, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so he mentioned a long story, the summary of which is: A beautiful woman in the time of the Children of Israel was approached by four of their leaders, but she refused each of them, so they agreed among themselves against her, and they testified against her before David, peace be upon him, that she had allowed a dog of hers to have sex with her, which he had become accustomed to doing to her, so he ordered her to be stoned. When it was the evening of that day, Solomon sat and young men like him gathered with him, so he stood up as a judge and four of them dressed up as those men, and another as a woman, and they testified against her that she had allowed a dog to have sex with her, so Solomon said, Separate them. So the first of them asked, What was the color of the dog? He said, Black, so he dismissed him and summoned the other and asked him about his color. He said, Red, and the other said, Dark, and the other said, White. So he ordered that they be killed. This was reported to David, peace be upon him, so he immediately summoned those four and asked them separately about the color of that dog. They disagreed with him, so he ordered that they be killed. And His saying: And We subjected with David the mountains, to glorify God, and the birds verse, and that was due to the sweetness of his voice when he recited His Book, the Psalms. When he chanted it, the birds would stand in the air and respond to him, and the mountains would respond to him in recitation. For this reason, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Abu Musa al-Ash’ari while he was reciting the Qur’an at night and he had a very sweet voice, he stopped and listened to his recitation and said: This man has been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David. He said: O Messenger of God, if I had known that you were listening, I would have praised it for you. Abu Uthman al-Nahdi said: I have never heard the sound of cymbals, strings, or flutes like the voice of Abu Musa, may God be pleased with him. Despite this, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David. And His statement: And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you, to protect you from your violence, meaning the making of armor. Qatada said: Before him, armor was only plates, and he was the first to string it into rings, as God Almighty said: “And We made iron soft for him, saying, ‘Make coats of mail and measure the links. ’” That is, do not make the ring too wide, lest the nail become loose, and do not make the nail too thick, lest the ring become loose. For this reason He said: To protect you from your violence, meaning in battle. Then will you be grateful? That is, for God’s blessings upon you when He inspired His servant David with it, and taught him that for your sake. And His statement: And to Solomon We subjected the wind, blowing violently means: We subjected to Solomon the wind, flowing by his command toward the land which We had blessed meaning the land of Ash-Sham and We are Knowing of all things. This is because he had a carpet of wood on which he placed everything he needed of the affairs of the kingdom, the horses, the camels, the tents, and the soldiers. Then he would command the wind to carry him, so it would enter under him, then carry him, raise him, and travel with him, and the birds would shade him, protecting him from the heat, to wherever he wished on the earth. Then he would dismount and his tools and his servants would be placed. God Almighty said: So We subjected to him the wind, blowing gently by his command wherever he desired. And God Almighty said: Its morning is a month and its evening is a month. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was reported on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Abu Sinan on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr who said: Six hundred thousand chairs were placed for Solomon, and the believing humans would sit on the one closest to him, then the believing jinn would sit behind them. Then he would command the birds to shade them, then he would command the wind to carry him, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair said: Solomon would command the wind and it would gather together like a huge mountain, then he would command his bed to be placed on the highest place on it, then he would call for a winged horse to rise until it climbed onto his bed, then he would command the wind to carry him to every high place below the sky, while he would lower his head, not turning right or left, out of glorification of God Almighty, and in gratitude for what he knew of the smallness of what he was in in the kingdom of God Almighty, until the wind placed him where it wished to place him. And His statement: And among the devils are those who dive for him meaning in the water, extracting pearls and jewels and other things, and they do work other than that meaning other than that, as God Almighty said: And the devils are all builders and divers * And others bound in chains. And His statement: And We were their guardians meaning God protects him from any of the devils harming him, rather each is in His grasp and under His control, none of them dares to approach him or come near him, rather He rules over them: if He wills He releases and if He wills He imprisons whomever He wishes of them, and for this reason He said: and others bound in chains.

So he judged in favor of the younger one.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs, and al-Nasa’i included it in a chapter in the Book of Judgment: Chapter on the judge who suggests contrary to the ruling in order to learn the truth. And thus the story that Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Solomon, peace be upon him, from his history, through Al-Hasan Ibn Sufyan, on the authority of Safwan Ibn Salih, on the authority of Al-Walid Ibn Muslim, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Bashir, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so he mentioned a long story, the summary of which is: A beautiful woman in the time of the Children of Israel was approached by four of their leaders, but she refused each of them, so they agreed among themselves against her, and they testified against her before David, peace be upon him, that she had allowed a dog of hers to have sex with her, which he had become accustomed to doing to her, so he ordered her to be stoned. When it was the evening of that day, Solomon sat and young men like him gathered with him, so he stood up as a judge and four of them dressed up as those men, and another as a woman, and they testified against her that she had allowed a dog to have sex with her, so Solomon said, Separate them. So the first of them asked, What was the color of the dog? He said, Black, so he dismissed him and summoned the other and asked him about his color. He said, Red, and the other said, Dark, and the other said, White. So he ordered that they be killed. This was reported to David, peace be upon him, so he immediately summoned those four and asked them separately about the color of that dog. They disagreed with him, so he ordered that they be killed. And His saying: And We subjected with David the mountains, to glorify God, and the birds verse, and that was due to the sweetness of his voice when he recited His Book, the Psalms. When he chanted it, the birds would stand in the air and respond to him, and the mountains would respond to him in recitation. For this reason, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Abu Musa al-Ash’ari while he was reciting the Qur’an at night and he had a very sweet voice, he stopped and listened to his recitation and said: This man has been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David. He said: O Messenger of God, if I had known that you were listening, I would have praised it for you. Abu Uthman al-Nahdi said: I have never heard the sound of cymbals, strings, or flutes like the voice of Abu Musa, may God be pleased with him. Despite this, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David. And His statement: And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you, to protect you from your violence, meaning the making of armor. Qatada said: Before him, armor was only plates, and he was the first to string it into rings, as God Almighty said: “And We made iron soft for him, saying, ‘Make coats of mail and measure the links. ’” That is, do not make the ring too wide, lest the nail become loose, and do not make the nail too thick, lest the ring become loose. For this reason He said: To protect you from your violence, meaning in battle. Then will you be grateful? That is, for God’s blessings upon you when He inspired His servant David with it, and taught him that for your sake. And His statement: And to Solomon We subjected the wind, blowing violently means: We subjected to Solomon the wind, flowing by his command toward the land which We had blessed meaning the land of Ash-Sham and We are Knowing of all things. This is because he had a carpet of wood on which he placed everything he needed of the affairs of the kingdom, the horses, the camels, the tents, and the soldiers. Then he would command the wind to carry him, so it would enter under him, then carry him, raise him, and travel with him, and the birds would shade him, protecting him from the heat, to wherever he wished on the earth. Then he would dismount and his tools and his servants would be placed. God Almighty said: So We subjected to him the wind, blowing gently by his command wherever he desired. And God Almighty said: Its morning is a month and its evening is a month. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was reported on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Abu Sinan on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr who said: Six hundred thousand chairs were placed for Solomon, and the believing humans would sit on the one closest to him, then the believing jinn would sit behind them. Then he would command the birds to shade them, then he would command the wind to carry him, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair said: Solomon would command the wind and it would gather together like a huge mountain, then he would command his bed to be placed on the highest place on it, then he would call for a winged horse to rise until it climbed onto his bed, then he would command the wind to carry him to every high place below the sky, while he would lower his head, not turning right or left, out of glorification of God Almighty, and in gratitude for what he knew of the smallness of what he was in in the kingdom of God Almighty, until the wind placed him where it wished to place him. And His statement: And among the devils are those who dive for him meaning in the water, extracting pearls and jewels and other things, and they do work other than that meaning other than that, as God Almighty said: And the devils are all builders and divers * And others bound in chains. And His statement: And We were their guardians meaning God protects him from any of the devils harming him, rather each is in His grasp and under His control, none of them dares to approach him or come near him, rather He rules over them: if He wills He releases and if He wills He imprisons whomever He wishes of them, and for this reason He said: and others bound in chains.
21:83: The Almighty mentions about Job, peace be upon him, what afflicted him in terms of his wealth, children and body. He had many animals, livestock and crops, and children and satisfactory homes. He was afflicted with all of that and it went away to the last. Then he was afflicted with leprosy in his body, it is said: with leprosy in the rest of his body, and nothing remained healthy except his heart and tongue, with which he would remember God Almighty, until his companions turned away from him, and he was isolated in a corner of the country, and no one remained to show mercy on him except his wife, who would take care of him. It is said: she was in need, so she began to serve the people for his sake. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The people most afflicted are the prophets, then the righteous, then the next best and the next best." And in another hadith: "A man is afflicted according to his religious commitment. If his religious commitment is firm, his affliction will increase." The Prophet of God, Job, peace be upon him, was the epitome of patience. He is an example of that. Yazid bin Maysarah said: When God tested Job, peace be upon him, with the loss of his family, wealth and children, and nothing remained for him, he praised him and said: I thank You, Lord of Lords, Who has been kind to me. You have given me wealth and children, and there is not a part of my heart that has not been entered by that. You have taken all of that from me, and emptied my heart, and nothing stands between me and You. If my enemy, Satan, knew what I did, he would envy me. Satan found something reprehensible about that. He said: And Job, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, You have given me wealth and children, and no one has ever come to my door to complain about the injustice I have done him, and You know that. And he used to make me lie down on the bed, but I left it, and I said to myself, O soul, you were not created to lie down on the bed. I left that only seeking Your pleasure. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. A long story has been narrated about Wahb ibn Munabbih in his account, which was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim with a chain of transmission on his authority, and it was mentioned by more than one of the later commentators, and it contains strange things that we have left out due to the length. It has been narrated that he remained in affliction for a long time, then they differed about the reason that prompted him to make this supplication. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Job, peace be upon him, was afflicted for seven years and months, lying on the rubbish heap of the Children of Israel, with animals swarming around his body, then God relieved him and gave him a great reward and praised him well. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He remained in the affliction for three years, neither increasing nor decreasing. Al-Suddi said: Job’s flesh fell off until nothing remained but the nerves and bones, so his wife would take care of him and bring him ashes to put in it. When his pain became prolonged, his wife said to him: O Job, if you would ask your Lord to relieve you. He said: I have lived for seventy years in good health, so it is little for God that I should be patient for him for seventy years. She was alarmed by that, so she went out and worked for the people for wages and brought him what she got and fed him. Then Satan went to two men from the people of Palestine, who were his friends and brothers. He went to them and said: Your brother Job has been afflicted with such and such a affliction, so go to him and visit him, and take with you some of the wine of your land, for if he drinks from it he will be cured. So they went to him and when they saw him they cried. He said: Who are you? They said: We are so-and-so and so-and-so. He welcomed them and said: Welcome to those who do not ignore me when afflicted. They said: O Job, perhaps you were concealing something and revealing something else, and that is why God tested you? He raised his head to the sky and said: He knows. I did not conceal anything and reveal something else, but my Lord tested me to see whether I would be patient or impatient. They said to him: O Job, drink from our wine, for if you drink from it you will be cured. He became angry and said: The wicked one came to you and ordered you to do this? Your speech, food and drink are forbidden to me. So they got up from him, and his wife went out to work for the people. She baked bread for a family who had a young boy, and made them a loaf of bread. Their son was asleep, and they did not want to wake him, so they gave him to her. She brought him to Job, but he disapproved of him and said: You did not bring me this, so what is the matter with you today? So she told him the story. He said: Perhaps the boy has woken up and asked for the loaf of bread but did not find it, so he is crying for his family. So go with him to him. So she came until she reached the people’s steps, and one of their sheep butted her. She said: Cursed is Job the sinner! When she went up, she found that the boy had woken up and was asking for the loaf of bread and crying for his family, not accepting anything from them except this. So she said: May God have mercy on him, meaning Job. So she gave him the loaf of bread and returned. Then Satan came to her in the form of a doctor and said to her: Your husband has been ill for a long time, so if he wants to recover, let him take a fly and slaughter it in the name of the idol of the Banu So-and-so, for he will recover and repent after that. So she said that to Job, and he said: “The evil one has come to you. By God, if you recover, I promise you that I will flog you a hundred lashes.” So she went out seeking him, but he withheld her sustenance, so she did not go to the people of a house who wanted her. When that became severe for her and she feared that Job would be hungry, she shaved a horn from her hair and sold it to a young girl from the daughters of the nobles, so they gave her food. She brought it to Job, but when he saw it he did not recognize it and said: Where did you get this from? She said: I worked for some people and they fed me, so he ate from it. The next day she went out and looked for work but could not find any, so she also shaved a horn and sold it to that slave girl, and they also gave her some of that food. She brought it to Job, but he said: By God, I will not eat it until I know where it is from. So she put down her veil, and when he saw her head shaved he was very upset, so at that time he called upon God Almighty and said: He called upon his Lord, ‘Indeed, distress has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.’ Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad told us, Abu Imran al-Joni told us on the authority of Nawf al-Bakali that the devil who ascended in Job was called Mabsoot. He said: Job’s wife used to say: Call upon God and He will heal you. But he did not call upon Him until a group of the Children of Israel passed by him. Some of them said to one another: What has befallen him has only befallen him because of a great sin he committed. Then he said: “He called upon his Lord: ‘Indeed, distress has seized me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.’” And my father told us, Abu Salamah told us, Jarir bin Hazim told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, who said: Job, peace be upon him, had two brothers. One day they came to him and could not get close to him because of his bad odor, so they stood from a distance. One of them said to the other: If God had known any good in Job, He would not have afflicted him with this. Job was alarmed by their words, as he had never been alarmed by anything before. He said: O God, if You know that I have never spent a night full while I know where someone is hungry, then believe me. So He was told the truth from the heavens, and they were listening. Then he said: O God, if You know that I have never had two shirts, and I know where someone is naked, then believe me. So He was told the truth from the heavens, and they were listening. Then he said: O God, by Your glory, then he fell down in prostration and said: O God, by Your glory, I will never raise my head until You uncover me. So he did not raise his head until He uncovered it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another chain of transmission with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a similar manner. He said: Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-A’la informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Nafi’ ibn Yazid informed me on the authority of ‘Aqeel on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The affliction of God’s Prophet Job lasted for eighteen years, and both those near and far rejected him, except for two men from among his brothers who were among his closest friends. They used to come to him in the morning and in the evening. One of them said to his companion: ‘By God, you know that Job has committed a sin that no one else in the world has committed.’ His companion said to him: ‘What is that?’ He said: ‘It has been eighteen years since God has shown him mercy and removed what is wrong with him.’ When they went to him, the man could not wait until he mentioned it to him. So Job (peace be upon him) said: ‘I do not know what you are saying, except that God the Almighty knows that I used to pass by two men who were arguing and mentioning God, so I would return to my house and expiate for them, hating that they mention God except in a right way.’ He said: ‘He would go out to fulfil his need, and when he had completed it, his wife would stay with him.’” And one day, it was delayed, so God revealed to Job in his place, Strike with your foot, this is a cool bath and a drink. This hadith is very strange. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad told us, Ali bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: And God clothed him in a garment from Paradise, so Job moved aside and sat in a corner, and his wife came and did not recognize him, so she said: O servant of God, where did this afflicted man who was here go? Perhaps the dogs or the wolves took him, so she began to talk to him for an hour. He said: Woe to you, I am Job. She said: Are you mocking me, O servant of God? He said: Woe to you, I am Job, God has returned my body to me, and Ibn Abbas said the same, and He returned to him his money and his children clearly and the same with them. And Wahb bin Munabbih said: God revealed to Job, I have returned to you your family and your money, and the same with them. Wash yourself with this water, for in it is your healing, and offer a sacrifice on behalf of your companions, and ask forgiveness for them, for they have disobeyed me regarding you. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. He also said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Amr ibn Marzuq told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Nadr ibn Anas, on the authority of Bashir ibn Nahik, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When God healed Job, He rained down golden locusts upon him. He began to take some of them in his hand and put them in his garment. It was said to him: O Job, are you not satisfied? He said: O Lord, and who is satisfied with Your mercy?” Its origin is in the two Sahihs and it will come in another place. And his saying: And We gave him his family and the like of them with them It was mentioned earlier from Ibn Abbas that he said: They were returned to him in person, and this is how Al-Awfi narrated it from Ibn Abbas also, and something similar was narrated from Ibn Masoud and Mujahid, and Al-Hasan and Qatadah said the same. Some of them claimed that the name of his wife was Rahmah, so if he took that from the context of the verse, then it is far from the right path, and if he took it from the transmission of the People of the Book and it was authenticated from them, then it is something that cannot be believed or denied, and Ibn Asakir named her in his history, may God Almighty have mercy on him: He said: And it is said that her name was Leah, daughter of Mansha bin Yusuf bin Ya’qub bin Ishaq bin Ibrahim, he said: And it is said that Leah, daughter of Ya’qub, peace be upon him, the wife of Job, was with him in the land of Al-Thaniyah, and Mujahid said: It was said to him: O Job, your family is yours in Paradise, so if you wish we will bring them to you, and if you wish we will leave them for you in Paradise and compensate you with the like of them? He said: No, rather leave them for me in Paradise, so they were left for him in Paradise and he was compensated with the like of them in this world. Hammad bin Zaid said on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni on the authority of Nawf Al-Bakali who said: He was given their reward in the Hereafter and given the same in this world. He said: So I told it to Mutraf, and he said: I did not know its meaning before today. And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Qatada, Al-Suddi and more than one of the Salaf, and God knows best. His statement: A mercy from Us means that We did that to him as a mercy from God to him. And a reminder for the worshippers means that We made him an example in that so that those who were afflicted would not think that We did that to them because they were insignificant to Us, and so that they would follow his example in being patient with the decrees of God and His testing of His servants with whatever He wills, and He has the utmost wisdom in that.

He began to take some of them in his hand and put them in his garment. It was said to him: O Job, are you not satisfied? He said: O Lord, and who is satisfied with Your mercy?” Its origin is in the two Sahihs and it will come in another place. And his saying: And We gave him his family and the like of them with them It was mentioned earlier from Ibn Abbas that he said: They were returned to him in person, and this is how Al-Awfi narrated it from Ibn Abbas also, and something similar was narrated from Ibn Masoud and Mujahid, and Al-Hasan and Qatadah said the same. Some of them claimed that the name of his wife was Rahmah, so if he took that from the context of the verse, then it is far from the right path, and if he took it from the transmission of the People of the Book and it was authenticated from them, then it is something that cannot be believed or denied, and Ibn Asakir named her in his history, may God Almighty have mercy on him: He said: And it is said that her name was Leah, daughter of Mansha bin Yusuf bin Ya’qub bin Ishaq bin Ibrahim, he said: And it is said that Leah, daughter of Ya’qub, peace be upon him, the wife of Job, was with him in the land of Al-Thaniyah, and Mujahid said: It was said to him: O Job, your family is yours in Paradise, so if you wish we will bring them to you, and if you wish we will leave them for you in Paradise and compensate you with the like of them? He said: No, rather leave them for me in Paradise, so they were left for him in Paradise and he was compensated with the like of them in this world. Hammad bin Zaid said on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni on the authority of Nawf Al-Bakali who said: He was given their reward in the Hereafter and given the same in this world. He said: So I told it to Mutraf, and he said: I did not know its meaning before today. And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Qatada, Al-Suddi and more than one of the Salaf, and God knows best. His statement: A mercy from Us means that We did that to him as a mercy from God to him. And a reminder for the worshippers means that We made him an example in that so that those who were afflicted would not think that We did that to them because they were insignificant to Us, and so that they would follow his example in being patient with the decrees of God and His testing of His servants with whatever He wills, and He has the utmost wisdom in that.
21:85: As for Ismail, what is meant by him is the son of Abraham, peace be upon them both. He was mentioned earlier in Surah Maryam, as was Idris, peace be upon him. As for Dhul-Kifl, it appears from the context that he was not paired with the prophets except that he was a prophet. Others said: He was a righteous man, a just king, and a fair judge. Ibn Jarir hesitated about that, and God knows best. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And Dhul-Kifl he said: A righteous man who was not a prophet. He promised a prophet of his people that he would take care of his people's affairs, establish them for him, and judge between them with justice. He did that, so he was called Dhul-Kifl. Ibn Abi Nujayh also narrated this on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Affan told us, Wahib told us, Dawud told us on the authority of Mujahid who said: When al-Yasa’ grew old, he said: If I were to appoint a man as my successor over the people to rule over them during my lifetime, so that I may see how he will act. So he gathered the people and said: Who will accept three things from me so that I may appoint him as my successor: He fasts during the day, prays at night, and does not get angry? A man whom people looked down upon stood up and said: I will. He said: You fast during the day, pray at night, and do not get angry? He said: Yes. He said: So he turned him back that day and said the same thing the next day, so the people remained silent. Then that man stood up and said: I will. So he appointed him as my successor. Iblis began to say to the devils: Go to so-and-so, but that exhausted them, so he said: Leave me and him. So he came to him in the form of an old, poor man. He came to him when he went to bed for the afternoon nap - and he did not sleep day or night except for that sleep - so he knocked on the door and said: Who is this? He said: An old man who has been wronged. He said: So he got up and opened the door and began to tell him the story. He said: There is a dispute between me and my people, and they have wronged me, and they did this and that to me. He kept on talking to him until the afternoon came and the afternoon was over. He said: When you go, come to me and I will take your right for you. So he went and left. He was in his council and began to look to see if he could see the old man, but he did not see him. So he got up and followed him. When the next day came, he began to judge between the people and wait for him, but he did not see him. When he returned to the afternoon and went to bed, he came to him and knocked on the door and said: Who is this? He said: The old oppressed sheikh. So he opened the door for him and said: Didn't I tell you, when you sit, to come to me? He said: They are the most wicked people. If they know that you are sitting, they say: We will give you your right, and if you stand, they deny me. He said: Go, and when you go, come to me. He said: So he missed the siesta, so he went and waited for it but did not see it, and drowsiness was difficult for him, so he said to some of his family: Do not let anyone approach this door until I sleep, for sleep is difficult for me. When that hour came, he came and the man said to him: Behind you, behind you. He said: I came to him yesterday and mentioned my situation to him, so he said: No, by God, we were ordered not to let anyone approach it. When he became tired, he looked and saw a window in the house, so he climbed through it, and behold, he was in the house, and behold, he was knocking on the door from inside. He said: The man woke up and said: O so-and-so, did I not order you? He said: By God, you were not given permission from me, so look from where you came. He said: So he went to the door and behold, it was closed as he closed it. And behold, the man was with him in the house and he recognized him, so he said: Are they enemies of God? He said: Yes, you exhausted me in everything, so I did what you see to anger you. So God called him Dhul-Kifl because he undertook a matter and fulfilled it. And thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Zuhair bin Ishaq on the authority of Dawud on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Yunus told us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Muslim, who said: Ibn Abbas said: There was a judge among the Children of Israel when death came to him, so he said: Who will take my place without getting angry? A man said: I will. So he was called Dhul-Kifl. He said: He would spend the whole night praying, then he would fast in the morning and judge between the people. He said: And he would have an hour to rest. He said: So it was like that, then Satan came to him while he was sleeping, and his companions said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: A poor man who has a right over a man, and he has overcome me over him. They said: Stay where you are until he wakes up. He said: And he was asleep. He said: So he started shouting deliberately until he woke him up. He said: So he heard him, and he said: What is the matter with you? He said: A poor man who has a right over a man. He said: Go and tell him that he will give you. He said: He has refused. He said: Go to him yourself. He left, then came back the next day and said: What is the matter with you? He said: I went to him, but he did not raise his head because of what you said. He said: Go to him and tell him to give you your right. So he went and came back the next day when he said that. His companions said to him: Go out, may God do to you. You come every day when he sleeps and do not let him sleep. He said: So he started shouting because I am a poor man. If I were rich, he would have heard it again and said: What is wrong with you? He said: I went to him and he hit me. He said: Walk until I come with you. He said: So he held his hand and when he saw him go with him, he threw his hand away from him and fled. And thus it was narrated from Abdullah bin Al-Harith, Muhammad bin Qais, Abu Hijra Al-Akbar and others from the Salaf, something similar to this story, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Jamahir told us, Saeed bin Bashir told us, Qatada told us on the authority of Kinanah bin al-Akhns, who said: I heard al-Ash’ari saying on this pulpit: Dhul-Kifl was not a prophet, but he was - meaning among the Children of Israel - a righteous man who prayed a hundred prayers every day, so Dhul-Kifl took responsibility for him after him, so he prayed a hundred prayers every day, so he was called Dhul-Kifl. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, who said: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari said, and he mentioned it as disconnected, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad narrated a strange hadith and said: Asbat bin Muhammad told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Sa’d, the freed slave of Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a hadith that if I had only heard it once or twice, he would count seven times, but I heard it more than that. He said: “Al-Kifl was from the Children of Israel and did not hesitate to commit a sin. A woman came to him and he gave her sixty dinars on condition that he would have intercourse with her. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, she trembled and cried. He said: What makes you cry? I forced you? She said: No, but this is an act that I have never done before, and need only compelled me to do it. He said: So you do this when you have never done it? Then he came down and said: Go with the dinars for yourself. Then he said: By God, Al-Kifl will never disobey God. So he died that night, and in the morning it was written on his door: God has forgiven Al-Kifl.” This is how it appears in this narration, Al-Kifl, without any addition, and God knows best. This hadith was not narrated by any of the authors of the six books, and its chain of transmission is strange, and in any case The wording of the hadith is that it is all of the guarantor, and it did not say Dhu al-Kifl, so perhaps it is another man, and God knows best.

21:87: This story is mentioned here and in Surat As-Saffat and in Surat Nun, and that is that Yunus bin Matta, peace be upon him, was sent by God to the people of the village of Nineveh, which is a village in the land of Mosul, so he called them to God Almighty, but they refused him and persisted in their disbelief, so he left them angry with them, and promised them punishment after three days, so when they were sure of that from him and knew that the prophet does not lie, they went out to the desert with their children, livestock and cattle, and separated the mothers from their children, then they supplicated to God Almighty and cried out to Him, and the camels and their young ones brayed, and the cows and their young moaned, and the sheep and their young bleated, so God lifted the punishment from them, God Almighty said: “Why was there not a city that believed and its faith benefited it except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time.” As for Yunus, peace be upon him, he went and boarded a ship with some people, but it went ashore with them. They feared that they would drown, so they cast lots for a man to throw in from among them to relieve themselves. The lot fell on Yunus, but they refused to throw him in. Then they cast lots again and it fell on him again, but they refused. Then they cast lots again and it fell on him again. God Almighty said: So he cast lots, and he was among those who were cast away. That is, the lot fell on him, so Yunus, peace be upon him, got up, stripped off his clothes, and threw himself into the sea. God Almighty sent from the Green Sea - according to what Ibn Masoud said - a whale that split the seas until it came and swallowed Yunus when he threw himself from the ship. God inspired that whale not to eat his flesh or crush his bones, for Yunus is not your provision, but your belly will be a prison for him. His saying: And Dhul-Nun means the whale, the addition to it is correct with this relation. And his saying: When he went off in anger Ad-Dahhak said to his al-Nas 114:He thought that We would not have power over him meaning that We would restrict him in the belly of the whale. Something similar to this is narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it and cited as evidence for it the saying of God Almighty: “And whoever has his provision restricted - let him spend from what God has given him. God does not charge a soul except [with that within] what He has given it. God will grant, after hardship, ease.” Atiyah Al-Awfi said: He thought that We would not have power over him meaning that We would decree it for him, as if he made that mean estimation, for the Arabs say: qadar and qadar have the same meaning, and the poet said: That time that has passed will not return. Blessed are you, whatever you can do will happen. You have the power. And from this is the saying of the Most High: So the waters met by a matter already predestined. That is, predestined. “Then he cried out in the darkness, ‘There is no god except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.’” Ibn Mas’ud said: The darkness of the belly of the whale, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the night. This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas, Amr ibn Maymun, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah. Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d said: The darkness of a whale in the belly of another whale in the darkness of the sea. Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, and others said: That is because the whale took him through the seas, splitting them open until it reached the bottom of the sea. Yunus heard the pebbles glorifying God in the depths of the sea. At that moment and there he said: “There is no god except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.” Awf Al-A’rabi said: When Yunus was in the belly of the whale, he thought that he had died, then he moved his feet, and when they moved, he prostrated in his place, then he called out, O Lord, I have taken for You a place of prostration in a place that no one else has reached. Saeed bin Abi Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: He stayed in the belly of the whale for forty days. Both were narrated by Ibn Jarir. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said on the authority of someone who told him on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, the freed slave of Umm Salamah: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God wanted to imprison Yunus in the belly of the whale, God revealed to the whale, ‘Take him and do not scratch his flesh or break his bones.’ When he reached the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound and said to himself, ‘What is this?’ God revealed to him while he was in the belly of the whale, ‘This is the glorification of sea creatures.’ He said, ‘And he glorified while he was in the belly of the whale,’ and the angels heard his glorification and said, ‘O our Lord, we hear a weak voice in a strange land.’ He said, ‘That is My servant Yunus. He disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the whale in the sea.’ They said, ‘The righteous servant from whom a righteous deed ascended to You every day and night?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ They interceded for him at that time, and He ordered the whale to throw him up on the shore, as God, the Most High, said, ‘And he was sick.’” Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and narrated by Al-Bazzar in His chain of transmission is on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he mentioned it in a similar manner, then he said: We do not know that it is narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except from this source with this chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Abu Ubaidullah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Akhi Ibn Wahb narrated to us, my uncle narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me that Yazid al-Raqashi said: I heard Anas ibn Malik, and I do not know except that Anas traces the hadith back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when the Prophet Yunus, peace be upon him, wanted to supplicate with these words while he was in the belly of the whale, he said: O God, there is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers. Then this supplication came from beneath the Throne, and the angels said: O Lord, a weak, well-known voice from a strange land. He said: Do you not know that? They said: No, O Lord, and who is he? He said: My servant Yunus. They said: Your servant Yunus, for whom accepted deeds and answered supplications have not ceased to be raised. They said: O Lord, will You not have mercy on what he used to do in times of ease and save him from affliction? He said: Yes. So He ordered the whale to throw him out into the open. And His saying: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress meaning We took him out of the belly of the whale and that darkness. And thus do We save the believers meaning if they are in hardships and call upon Us, turning to Us, especially if they call upon this supplication in a state of affliction, for the encouragement to call upon Him with this supplication came from the Master of the Prophets. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail bin Omar told us, Yunus bin Abi Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Saad told us, my father Muhammad told me on the authority of his father Saad, he is the son of Abi Waqqas, may God be pleased with him, he said: “I passed by Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, in the mosque, and I greeted him, and he looked at me intently but did not return my greeting, so I went to Umar bin Al-Khattab and said: O Commander of the Faithful, has anything happened in Islam, twice? He said: No, and what is that? I said no, except that I passed by Uthman just now in the mosque and greeted him, and he looked at me intently but did not return my greeting. He said: So Umar sent for Uthman and summoned him, and said: What prevented you from returning your brother’s greeting? He said: I did not. Saad said: I said yes until he swore and I swore. He said: Then Uthman remembered and said: Yes, and I seek forgiveness from God and I repent to Him. You passed by me just now while I was thinking about a word I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. No, by God, I have never mentioned it without my sight and heart being covered with a veil.” Sa`d said: “Then I will tell you about it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned to us the first supplication. Then a Bedouin came and distracted him until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up, so I followed him. When I feared that he would precede me to his home, I stamped my feet on the ground. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned to me and said: ‘Who is this, Abu Ishaq?’ I said: ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Then who is he?’ I said: ‘No, by God, except that you mentioned to us the first supplication. Then this Bedouin came and distracted you. He said: ‘Yes, it is the supplication of Dhul-Nun when he was in the belly of the whale: “There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.” For no Muslim has ever supplicated to his Lord with it for anything except that He has answered him.’” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i in Al-Yawm wal-Laylah from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sa`d on the authority of his father Sa`d. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar narrated to us, on the authority of Katheer bin Zaid, on the authority of Al-Muttalib bin Hantab. Abu Khalid said: I think it was on the authority of Mus’ab, meaning Ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Sa’d, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever supplicates with the supplication of Yunus, his supplication will be answered. Abu Saeed said: He meant by it: And thus do We save the believers. Ibn Jarir said: Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i narrated to me, Yahya bin Salih narrated to us, Abu Yahya bin Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, Bishr bin Mansour narrated to me, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The name of God by which if He is supplicated, He answers, and if He is asked by it, He gives. The supplication of Yunus bin Matta.” I said: O Messenger of God, is it for Yunus specifically or for all Muslims? He said: “It is specifically for Jonah bin Matta, and for the group of believers in general, if they call upon Him with it. Have you not heard the saying of God Almighty: ‘Then he called out in the darkness, “There is no god except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.” So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.’ It is a condition from God for whoever calls upon Him with it.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj told us, Dawud ibn al-Muhbar ibn Qahdham al-Maqdisi told us on the authority of Kathir ibn Ma’bad who said: I asked al-Hasan and said: O Abu Saeed, what is the greatest name of God by which if He is called upon, He answers, and if He is asked by it, He gives? He said: My nephew, do you not read the Qur’an, the words of God the Most High: “And Dhul-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree anything upon him, so he called out within the darknesses, ‘There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.’ So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.” My nephew, this is the greatest name of God by which if He is called upon, He answers, and if He is asked by it, He gives.
21:88: This story is mentioned here and in Surat As-Saffat and in Surat Nun, and that is that Yunus bin Matta, peace be upon him, was sent by God to the people of the village of Nineveh, which is a village in the land of Mosul, so he called them to God Almighty, but they refused him and persisted in their disbelief, so he left them angry with them, and promised them punishment after three days, so when they were sure of that from him and knew that the prophet does not lie, they went out to the desert with their children, livestock and cattle, and separated the mothers from their children, then they supplicated to God Almighty and cried out to Him, and the camels and their young ones brayed, and the cows and their young moaned, and the sheep and their young bleated, so God lifted the punishment from them, God Almighty said: “Why was there not a city that believed and its faith benefited it except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time.” As for Yunus, peace be upon him, he went and boarded a ship with some people, but it went ashore with them. They feared that they would drown, so they cast lots for a man to throw in from among them to relieve themselves. The lot fell on Yunus, but they refused to throw him in. Then they cast lots again and it fell on him again, but they refused. Then they cast lots again and it fell on him again. God Almighty said: So he cast lots, and he was among those who were cast away. That is, the lot fell on him, so Yunus, peace be upon him, got up, stripped off his clothes, and threw himself into the sea. God Almighty sent from the Green Sea - according to what Ibn Masoud said - a whale that split the seas until it came and swallowed Yunus when he threw himself from the ship. God inspired that whale not to eat his flesh or crush his bones, for Yunus is not your provision, but your belly will be a prison for him. His saying: And Dhul-Nun means the whale, the addition to it is correct with this relation. And his saying: When he went off in anger Ad-Dahhak said to his al-Nas 114:He thought that We would not have power over him meaning that We would restrict him in the belly of the whale. Something similar to this is narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it and cited as evidence for it the saying of God Almighty: “And whoever has his provision restricted - let him spend from what God has given him. God does not charge a soul except [with that within] what He has given it. God will grant, after hardship, ease.” Atiyah Al-Awfi said: He thought that We would not have power over him meaning that We would decree it for him, as if he made that mean estimation, for the Arabs say: qadar and qadar have the same meaning, and the poet said: That time that has passed will not return. Blessed are you, whatever you can do will happen. You have the power. And from this is the saying of the Most High: So the waters met by a matter already predestined. That is, predestined. “Then he cried out in the darkness, ‘There is no god except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.’” Ibn Mas’ud said: The darkness of the belly of the whale, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the night. This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas, Amr ibn Maymun, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah. Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d said: The darkness of a whale in the belly of another whale in the darkness of the sea. Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, and others said: That is because the whale took him through the seas, splitting them open until it reached the bottom of the sea. Yunus heard the pebbles glorifying God in the depths of the sea. At that moment and there he said: “There is no god except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.” Awf Al-A’rabi said: When Yunus was in the belly of the whale, he thought that he had died, then he moved his feet, and when they moved, he prostrated in his place, then he called out, O Lord, I have taken for You a place of prostration in a place that no one else has reached. Saeed bin Abi Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: He stayed in the belly of the whale for forty days. Both were narrated by Ibn Jarir. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said on the authority of someone who told him on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, the freed slave of Umm Salamah: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God wanted to imprison Yunus in the belly of the whale, God revealed to the whale, ‘Take him and do not scratch his flesh or break his bones.’ When he reached the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound and said to himself, ‘What is this?’ God revealed to him while he was in the belly of the whale, ‘This is the glorification of sea creatures.’ He said, ‘And he glorified while he was in the belly of the whale,’ and the angels heard his glorification and said, ‘O our Lord, we hear a weak voice in a strange land.’ He said, ‘That is My servant Yunus. He disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the whale in the sea.’ They said, ‘The righteous servant from whom a righteous deed ascended to You every day and night?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ They interceded for him at that time, and He ordered the whale to throw him up on the shore, as God, the Most High, said, ‘And he was sick.’” Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and narrated by Al-Bazzar in His chain of transmission is on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he mentioned it in a similar manner, then he said: We do not know that it is narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except from this source with this chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Abu Ubaidullah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Akhi Ibn Wahb narrated to us, my uncle narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me that Yazid al-Raqashi said: I heard Anas ibn Malik, and I do not know except that Anas traces the hadith back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when the Prophet Yunus, peace be upon him, wanted to supplicate with these words while he was in the belly of the whale, he said: O God, there is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers. Then this supplication came from beneath the Throne, and the angels said: O Lord, a weak, well-known voice from a strange land. He said: Do you not know that? They said: No, O Lord, and who is he? He said: My servant Yunus. They said: Your servant Yunus, for whom accepted deeds and answered supplications have not ceased to be raised. They said: O Lord, will You not have mercy on what he used to do in times of ease and save him from affliction? He said: Yes. So He ordered the whale to throw him out into the open. And His saying: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress meaning We took him out of the belly of the whale and that darkness. And thus do We save the believers meaning if they are in hardships and call upon Us, turning to Us, especially if they call upon this supplication in a state of affliction, for the encouragement to call upon Him with this supplication came from the Master of the Prophets. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail bin Omar told us, Yunus bin Abi Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Saad told us, my father Muhammad told me on the authority of his father Saad, he is the son of Abi Waqqas, may God be pleased with him, he said: “I passed by Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, in the mosque, and I greeted him, and he looked at me intently but did not return my greeting, so I went to Umar bin Al-Khattab and said: O Commander of the Faithful, has anything happened in Islam, twice? He said: No, and what is that? I said no, except that I passed by Uthman just now in the mosque and greeted him, and he looked at me intently but did not return my greeting. He said: So Umar sent for Uthman and summoned him, and said: What prevented you from returning your brother’s greeting? He said: I did not. Saad said: I said yes until he swore and I swore. He said: Then Uthman remembered and said: Yes, and I seek forgiveness from God and I repent to Him. You passed by me just now while I was thinking about a word I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. No, by God, I have never mentioned it without my sight and heart being covered with a veil.” Sa`d said: “Then I will tell you about it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned to us the first supplication. Then a Bedouin came and distracted him until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up, so I followed him. When I feared that he would precede me to his home, I stamped my feet on the ground. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned to me and said: ‘Who is this, Abu Ishaq?’ I said: ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Then who is he?’ I said: ‘No, by God, except that you mentioned to us the first supplication. Then this Bedouin came and distracted you. He said: ‘Yes, it is the supplication of Dhul-Nun when he was in the belly of the whale: “There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.” For no Muslim has ever supplicated to his Lord with it for anything except that He has answered him.’” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i in Al-Yawm wal-Laylah from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sa`d on the authority of his father Sa`d. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar narrated to us, on the authority of Katheer bin Zaid, on the authority of Al-Muttalib bin Hantab. Abu Khalid said: I think it was on the authority of Mus’ab, meaning Ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Sa’d, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever supplicates with the supplication of Yunus, his supplication will be answered. Abu Saeed said: He meant by it: And thus do We save the believers. Ibn Jarir said: Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i narrated to me, Yahya bin Salih narrated to us, Abu Yahya bin Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, Bishr bin Mansour narrated to me, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The name of God by which if He is supplicated, He answers, and if He is asked by it, He gives. The supplication of Yunus bin Matta.” I said: O Messenger of God, is it for Yunus specifically or for all Muslims? He said: “It is specifically for Jonah bin Matta, and for the group of believers in general, if they call upon Him with it. Have you not heard the saying of God Almighty: ‘Then he called out in the darkness, “There is no god except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.” So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.’ It is a condition from God for whoever calls upon Him with it.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj told us, Dawud ibn al-Muhbar ibn Qahdham al-Maqdisi told us on the authority of Kathir ibn Ma’bad who said: I asked al-Hasan and said: O Abu Saeed, what is the greatest name of God by which if He is called upon, He answers, and if He is asked by it, He gives? He said: My nephew, do you not read the Qur’an, the words of God the Most High: “And Dhul-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree anything upon him, so he called out within the darknesses, ‘There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.’ So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.” My nephew, this is the greatest name of God by which if He is called upon, He answers, and if He is asked by it, He gives.
21:89: God the Almighty tells about His servant Zachariah when he asked God to grant him a son who would be a prophet after him. The story was presented in detail at the beginning of Surah Maryam and also in Surah Al Imran. Here is a brief summary of it: When he called upon his Lord, that is, secretly from his people, My Lord, leave me not alone, that is, I have no children or heir to rise up among the people after me, and You are the best of inheritors, a supplication and praise appropriate to the question. God the Almighty said: So We responded to him and granted him John and made his wife good for him, that is, his wife. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Saeed bin Jubair said: She was barren and could not bear children, so she gave birth. Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi said on the authority of Talha bin Amr on the authority of Ata’: There was a long tongue, so God made her good. In another narration: There was something wrong with her nature, so God made her good. Muhammad bin Ka’b and al-Suddi said the same, and the first context is more apparent. And His statement: Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds meaning in performing acts of worship and obedience. And they used to supplicate Us in hope and fear. Ath-Thawri said: Desiring what is with Us and in fear of what is with Us. And they were humbly submissive to Us. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, meaning believing in what God has revealed. Mujahid said: True believers. Abu al-Aaliyah said: Fearful. Abu Sinan said: Humility is the fear that is inherent in the heart and never leaves it. Mujahid also said: Humbling, meaning humble. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said: Humbling, meaning submissive to God Almighty. All of these statements are close. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Muhammad At-Tanafisi told us, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, Abdur-Rahman ibn Ishaq told us on the authority of Abdullah Al-Qurashi on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hakim who said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, delivered a sermon to us. Then he said: As for what comes after, I advise you to fear God, and to praise Him as He deserves, and to mix desire with fear, and to combine persistence with asking, for God Almighty praised Zachariah and his family, saying: Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.

21:91: Thus, the Almighty mentions the story of Mary and her son Jesus, peace be upon them, coupled with the story of Zachariah and his son John, peace be upon them. He first mentions the story of Zachariah, then follows it with the story of Mary, because that is connected to the other, as it is the creation of a child from an old man who had reached advanced age, and from an old barren woman who had not given birth in her youth. Then He mentions the story of Mary, which is more amazing, as it is the creation of a child from a female without a male. This is how it occurs in Surat Al Imran and in Surat Maryam. Here, He mentioned the story of Zachariah, then followed it with the story of Mary, saying: And she who guarded her chastity, meaning Mary, peace be upon her, as He said in Surat al-Tahrim 66:And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit. And His statement, And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds, meaning an indication that God is capable of everything, and that He creates whatever He wills, and that His command when He wills something is only to say to it, Be, and it is. This is like His statement, And We made him a sign for the people. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Umar ibn Ali told us, Abu Asim al-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Shu’ayb, meaning Ibn Bishr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, for the worlds, he said: The worlds are the jinn and mankind.
21:92: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Qatadah, and Abdurrahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said about His statement: Indeed, this nation of yours is one nation meaning: your religion is one religion. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said about this verse: He explains to them what they should fear and what they should do. Then he said: Indeed, this nation of yours is one nation meaning your way is one way. So his statement: Indeed, this is if and its subject, and your nation is the predicate of if, meaning this is your law that has been explained to you and clarified to you. And his statement: one nation is an accusative of state, and for this reason he said: And I am your Lord, so worship Me as he said: "O messengers, eat from the good things and work righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing. * And indeed, this nation of yours is one nation, and I am your Lord, so fear Me" and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We, the community of prophets, are children of one religion meaning that what is meant is the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, with various laws for His messengers, as God, the Most High, said: For each of you We prescribed a law and a method. And His statement: And their affair was divided among themselves means that the nations differed over their messengers, so some believed in them and some denied them. That is why He said: All will return to Us meaning on the Day of Resurrection, so each will be rewarded according to his deeds, if good then good and if evil then evil. That is why He said: So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer meaning his heart believes and he does righteous deeds there will be no denial for his effort like His statement: Indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of anyone who does good deeds meaning his effort, which is his work, will not be denied, rather he will be thanked and will not be wronged even by the weight of an atom. That is why He said: And indeed, We are for him recorders meaning He will record all of his deeds and nothing of them will be lost.

21:95: God Almighty says: "And it is forbidden for a town." Ibn Abbas said: It is obligatory, meaning it has been decreed that the people of every town that was destroyed will not return to the world before the Day of Resurrection. This is what Ibn Abbas, Abu Ja`far al-Baqir, Qatadah and more than one person stated. And in a narration from Ibn Abbas: That they will not return, meaning they will not repent. The first statement is more apparent, and God knows best. And His saying: Until when Gog and Magog are let loose We have already mentioned that they are from the lineage of Adam, peace be upon him, and they are also from the lineage of Noah, from the children of Japheth, meaning the father of the Turks, and the Turks are a group of them who were left behind the dam that Dhul-Qarnayn built, and he said: “This is a mercy from my Lord, but when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is true. And We will leave some of them that Day surging against others” verse. And He said in this noble verse: Until when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they rush from every mound verse. That is, they hasten to walk towards corruption, and the mound is the high part of the earth, as Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Abu Salih, Ath-Thawri and others said. And this is their description when they come out, as if the listener is witnessing that. And none can inform you like the All-Knowing verse. This is the information of the All-Knowing of what was and what will be, the One who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but Him. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Yazid, who said: Ibn Abbas saw some children jumping on each other and playing, so Ibn Abbas said: This is how Gog and Magog will emerge, and mention of their emergence has been made in many hadiths of the Prophetic Sunnah. The first hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Asim bin Amr bin Qatada, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Gog and Magog will be opened, and they will come out upon the people, as God the Almighty said: ‘And they will come down from every hill.’ They will overwhelm the people, and the Muslims will withdraw from them to their cities and fortresses, and they will gather their livestock with them, and they will drink the waters of the earth, until some of them will pass by a river and drink what is in it until they leave it dry, until those after them will pass by that river and say: There was once water here, until no one remains of the people except someone in a fortress or city, and their speaker will say: These are the people of the earth, we have finished with them, and the people of heaven remain. He said: Then one of them will shake his spear, then throw it into the sky, and it will return to him stained with blood, as a affliction and trial. While they are like that, God the Almighty will send worms in… Their necks will be like locusts that emerge from their necks. They will become dead and no sound will be heard from them. The Muslims will say: Is there not a man who will sell himself for us and see what this enemy has done? He said: A man from among them will strip himself, thinking that he has prepared himself for death. He will go down and find them dead, one on top of the other. He will call out: O group of Muslims, do you not rejoice? God, the Almighty, has sufficed you against your enemy? They will leave their cities and fortresses and let their livestock go free, and they will have no grazing except their own flesh. You will be thanked for them as you have been thanked for any plant that you have ever eaten. Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Yunus ibn Bakir, from Ibn Ishaq.
