O servants of God, be steadfast.’ We said: ‘O Messenger of God, how long will he remain on earth?’ He said: ‘Forty days, one day like a year, one day like a month, one day like a week, and the rest of his days like your days.’ We said: ‘O Messenger of God, then that is the day that is…’” As a Sunnah, is it sufficient for us to pray one day and one night? He said: Do not estimate its value. We said: O Messenger of God, what is its speed on the earth? He said: Like rain that the wind blows strongly. He said: It passes by a neighborhood and calls them and they respond to it. Then he orders the sky to rain, and the earth to produce vegetation, and their livestock come to them with their highest peaks, their flanks extended, and their udders full. Then he passes by a neighborhood and calls them and they respond to his words, and their wealth follows him and they become destitute and have nothing of their wealth. Then he passes by a ruin and says to it: Bring forth your treasures, and its treasures follow him like swarms of bees. He said: Then he orders a man to be killed, so he strikes him with the sword and cuts him into two pieces, like a target shot. Then he calls him and he comes to him. While they are in that state, God the Almighty sends the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, and he descends at the white minaret east of Damascus between two Mahrouds, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. He follows him and catches up with him and kills him at the eastern gate of Ludd. He said: While they were like that, God the Almighty revealed to Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, “I have brought forth servants from among My servants whom you will not be able to fight. So take My servants to Mount Tur, and God the Almighty will send Gog and Magog, as He the Almighty said: “And they will rush from every hill.” So Jesus and his companions will ask God the Almighty, and He will send upon them a stench on their necks, and they will die as one person dies. Then Jesus and his companions will descend and they will not find a house on earth except that it has been filled with their stench and stench. So Jesus and his companions will ask God the Almighty, and God will send upon them birds like the necks of camels, and they will carry them and throw them wherever God wills. Ibn Jabir said: Ata’ bin Yazid al-Sakaski told me on the authority of Ka’b or someone else who said: They will throw them into the vagina. Ibn Jabir said: So I said, O Abu Yazid, where is the vagina? He said: The rising of the sun. He said: And God will send rain from which no house of mud or hair will be protected for forty days, and it will wash the earth until it leaves it like slippery ground, and it will be said to the earth: Grow your fruit and receive your blessing. He said: On that day, a group of people will eat from a pomegranate and seek shade under its hull, and the Messengers will be blessed until a she-camel will suffice a group of people, and a she-camel will suffice a thigh, and a sheep will suffice a household. He said: While they are like that, God the Almighty will send a pleasant wind that will take them under their armpits and will take the soul of every Muslim - or he said: every believer - and the worst of people will remain, fighting like donkeys, and the Hour will come upon them. Muslim alone transmitted it, not Al-Bukhari, and he and the rest of the people of Sunan transmitted it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jabir. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. The third hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Ibn Harmalah, on the authority of his aunt, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon while he was bandaging his finger from a scorpion sting, and he said: ‘You say you have no enemy, but you will continue to fight an enemy until Gog and Magog come: broad-faced, small-eyed, with reddish hair, swarming from every side as if their faces were hammered shields.’” And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Khalid ibn Abdullah ibn Harmalah al-Mudlaji, on the authority of his aunt, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it in the same manner. The fourth hadith It was mentioned at the end of the interpretation of Surat Al-A’raf from the narration of Imam Ahmad on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-A’wam, on the authority of Jabalah bin Suhaim, on the authority of Muthadd bin Amara, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “On the night of my Night Journey, I met Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them. He said: They discussed the matter of the Hour, so they referred their matter to Abraham, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. They referred their matter to Moses, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. They referred their matter to Jesus, and he said: As for its occurrence, no one knows about it except God. And what my Lord has entrusted to me is that the Antichrist will emerge with two sticks with me, and when he sees me he will melt like lead melts. He said: God will destroy him when he sees me, until even the rocks and trees will say: O Muslim, there is an unbeliever beneath me, so come and kill him. He said: God will destroy them, then the people will return to their lands and homelands. He said: At that time, Gog and Magog will emerge, and they will swarm from every hill, and they will tread on…” Their country, and they do not come upon anything except that they destroy it, and they do not pass by water except that they drink it - he said - then the people return to me complaining about them, so I call upon God against them and He destroys them and causes them to die until the earth empties from the stench of their stench, and God sends down rain that sweeps away their bodies until He throws them into the sea. So what my Lord has entrusted to me is that if that is the case, the Hour will be like a pregnant woman who has just given birth, and her family does not know when she will surprise them with her child, by night or by day.” It was narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Al-Awam ibn Hawshab, with a similar chain of transmission. He added: Al-Awam said: Verification of that was found in the Book of God Almighty: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they stream down from every mound. Ibn Jarir narrated it here from the hadith of Jabalah with it. The hadiths on this are very numerous, as are the reports from the Salaf. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Muammar from more than one person, from Hamid bin Hilal, from Abu Al-Saif, who said: Kaab said: When Gog and Magog come out, they dig until those around them hear the clatter of their axes. Then, when night falls, God casts into the tongue of one of them saying: We will come tomorrow and emerge, so God will restore it as it was. They come the next day and find that God has restored it as it was, so they dig until those around them hear the clatter of their axes. Then, when night falls, God casts into the tongue of one of them saying: We will come tomorrow and emerge, God willing. They come the next day and find it as they left it. They dig until they emerge. The first group passes by the lake and drinks its water. Then, the second group passes by and licks its mud. Then, the third group passes by and they say: There was once water here. The people flee from them and nothing can stand up to them. Then, they shoot their arrows into the sky and they return to them stained with blood. They say: We have defeated the people of the earth and the people of the sky. The sky, and Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, will call upon them, saying: O God, we have no power or ability to deal with them, so suffice us with whatever You will. Then God will send upon them a worm called Al-Naghf, which will tear their necks apart, and God will send upon them birds that will seize them with their beaks and throw them into the sea, and God will send a spring called Al-Hayat, and God will purify the earth and cause it to grow, so that even a pomegranate will satisfy the inhabitants. It was said: What is the inhabitants, O Ka’b? He said: The people of the house. He said: While the people are like that, a cry will come to them that Dhu Al-Sawiqatayn wants him. He said: Then Jesus, son of Mary, will send a vanguard of seven hundred or between seven hundred and eight hundred, until when they are on the way, God will send a pleasant Yemeni wind, and in it the soul of every believer will be taken. Then the dust of the people will remain, and they will copulate as animals copulate. So the Hour is like a man who circles around his horse when it gives birth. Ka’b said: Whoever says something after I say this or after I know this, he is an impostor. This is one of the best narrations of Ka’b Al-Ahbar, because of the authentic narrations that testify to him. It has been proven in the hadith that Jesus, son of Mary, will perform Hajj to the Ancient House. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, Imran told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Utbah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They will perform Hajj to this House and perform Umrah after the emergence of Gog and Magog. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it. His statement: And the true promise has drawn near means the Day of Resurrection when these horrors, earthquakes and calamities occur. The Hour has drawn near and when it comes and occurs, the disbelievers will say: This is a difficult day. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Then the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror meaning from the severity of what they witness of the great matters. Woe to us meaning they will say, Woe to us! We were indeed heedless of this meaning in this world. Rather, we were wrongdoers they will admit their wrongdoing to themselves when that will not benefit them.
21:98: God the Almighty says, addressing the people of Mecca, the polytheists of Quraysh and those who followed their religion from the worshippers of idols and statues: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. Ibn Abbas said: meaning its fuel, as He said: Its fuel is men and stones. Ibn Abbas also said: Fuel for Hell means the trees of Hell. In another narration he said: Fuel for Hell meaning firewood for Hell in Zanjiyah. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: its firewood, and it is likewise in the reading of Ali and Aisha, may God be pleased with them. Ad-Dahhak said: Fuel for Hell means what is thrown into it, and others said the same, and all are close. And His statement: You will be entering it means entering. If these were gods, they would not have entered it meaning if these idols and rivals that you have taken besides God were true gods, they would not have entered the Fire nor would they have entered it. And all are therein abiding eternally meaning the worshippers and their idols are all therein abiding eternally. For them therein is a sigh as God Almighty said: For them therein is a sigh and a sob and the sigh is the exit of their breath, and the sob is the entry of their breath and they therein do not hear. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Ibn Fadil told us, Abd al-Rahman, meaning al-Mas’udi, told us on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Mas’ud said: When those who remain will remain in Hell forever, they will be placed in coffins of fire with nails of fire in them, and none of them will see that he is being tortured in Hell except him. Then Abdullah recited: Therein they will have sighing, and therein they will not hear. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad on the authority of al-Mas’udi on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, and he mentioned it. And His statement: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us Ikrimah said: Mercy. And others said: Happiness. Those will be removed from it When God the Almighty mentioned the people of the Fire and their punishment because of their associating partners with God, He followed it up by mentioning the happy ones from among the believers in God and His Messengers, and they are those for whom happiness has preceded from God and who performed righteous deeds in this world, as God the Almighty said: For those who do good is the best and more and He said: Is the reward for good [anything] but good? So as they did good deeds in this world, God made their final destination and reward good, and saved them from the punishment and they obtained a great reward, so He said: “Those will be removed from it. They will not hear its hissing” meaning its burning in the bodies. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Ammar told us, Affan told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Al-Hariri on the authority of Abu Uthman, They will not hear its hissing sound, he said: A snake on the path stings them, and when it stings them, it says, His, hiss. And His statement, And they will abide in that which their souls desire, means that He saved them from what is forbidden and what is feared, and they obtained what they desired and loved. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj told us, Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Abi Yazid Al-Hamadani told us on the authority of Laith ibn Abi Sulaym on the authority of the cousin of Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir on the authority of Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, who said: He was talking with Ali one night, and he recited, Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it, he said: I am one of them, and Umar is one of them, and Uthman is one of them, and Al-Zubayr is one of them, and Talhah is one of them, and Abd Al-Rahman is one of them, or he said: Saad is one of them, he said: The prayer was called, so he stood up and I think he was dragging his garment while saying: They will not hear its hissing sound. Shu`bah said on the authority of Abu Bishr on the authority of Yusuf al-Makki on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hattab who said: I heard Ali say regarding His statement: Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us he said: Uthman and his companions. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Yusuf ibn Sa`d, and he is not Ibn Mahk on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hattab on the authority of Ali, so he mentioned it and his wording is Uthman from them. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it so those are the friends of God who will pass over the bridge faster than lightning, and the disbelievers will remain on their knees in it, so this is consistent with what we mentioned. Others said: Rather, it was revealed as an exception from the worshipped ones, and Ezra and the Messiah were excluded from them, as Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A`war said on the authority of Ibn Jurayj and Uthman ibn Ata’ on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will enter it then he made an exception and said: Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us it is said: They are the angels and Jesus, and the like. This is what is worshipped besides God, the Almighty, and this is what Ikrimah, Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj said. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us he said: It was revealed about Jesus, son of Mary, and Ezra, peace be upon them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Husayn ibn Isa ibn Maysarah told us, Abu Zuhair told us, Saad ibn Tarif told us, on the authority of Al-Asbagh, on the authority of Ali regarding His statement: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us he said: Everything that is worshipped besides God will be in the Fire except the sun, the moon and Jesus, son of Mary. Its chain of transmission is weak. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: Those will be removed from it he said: Jesus, Ezra and the angels. Ad-Dahhak said: Jesus, Mary, the angels, the sun, and the moon. This was also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Abu Salih, and others. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated a very strange hadith on this matter. He said: Al-Fadl bin Ya’qub Al-Rukhani told us, Saeed bin Muslimah bin Abdul Malik told us, Al-Layth bin Abi Salim told us, on the authority of Mughith, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. He said: Jesus, Ezra, and the angels. Some of them mentioned the story of Ibn Al-Zubayri and the debate with the polytheists. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Sahl told us, Muhammad bin Hassan Al-Anmati told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Arara told us, Yazid bin Abi Hakim told us, Al-Hakam, meaning Ibn Aban, told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: You claim that God revealed this verse to you: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. You will be removed from it.” We are coming, Ibn al-Zubayri said: "You have worshipped the sun, the moon, the angels, Ezra, and Jesus, son of Mary. Are all of these in the fire with our gods?" Then the verse was revealed: “And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from him. And they say, ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’ They only cite him to you out of argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. Narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah in his book Al-Ahadith Al-Mukhtara. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, Sufyan - meaning Al-Thawri - told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of his companions, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse was revealed: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will surely enter it, the polytheists said: So the angels, Ezra, and Jesus are worshipping besides God, so the verse was revealed: If these were gods, they would not have entered it, the gods that they worship, and all will abide therein eternally. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu Kudaynah, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he said: Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, may God have mercy on him, said in the Book of the Biography: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat one day with Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira in the mosque, then Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the mosque were more than one man from Quraysh, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke, and Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith came to him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to him until he silenced him, and he recited to him and them: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be brought to it. If these were gods, they would not have come to it. All will abide therein eternally. Therein they will have sighing, and therein they will not hear.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayri Al-Sahmi came and sat with them. Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira said to Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayri: By God, Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith did not stand up for Ibn Abdul Muttalib just now nor did he sit down, and Muhammad has claimed that I and what we worship of these gods of ours are fuel for Hell. Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayri said: By God, if I had found him, I would have argued with him. So ask Muhammad, everything that is worshipped besides God is in Hell with those who worship it, for we worship the angels. The Jews worship Ezra, and the Christians worship Christ Jesus, son of Mary. Al-Walid and those who were with him in the assembly were amazed at the words of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri, and they saw that he had argued and argued. So he mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “Whoever loves to be worshipped other than God is with those who worship Him. They only worship Satan and the one who commanded them to worship him.” And God revealed: “Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. They will not hear its hissing, and they will abide in that which their souls desire.” That is, Jesus and Ezra and those who worshipped from the rabbis and monks who continued in obedience to God, so those who worshipped them from the people of misguidance took them as lords other than God. And it was revealed regarding what they mentioned that they worshipped the angels and that they were the daughters of God: “And they said, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son. Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants.’” until His saying: “And whoever among them says, ‘I am a god other than Him,’ We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.” And it was revealed regarding what was mentioned regarding the matter of Jesus and that he is worshipped other than God. Al-Walid and those who were present with him were amazed. His argument and his argument: “And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, behold, your people turned away from him. And they said, ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’ They only cite him to you for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people. He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could have made from you angels on earth, succeeding [them].” And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour, so have no doubt about it. That is, the signs that were placed at his hands, such as reviving the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient evidence of knowledge of the Hour. He says: “So have no doubt about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.” And what Ibn al-Zubayri said is a great mistake, because the verse was revealed as an address to the people of Mecca regarding their worship of idols that are inanimate and do not have reason, so that it would be a rebuke and rebuke to their worshippers. For this reason, he said: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. So how can this be used against the Messiah, Ezra, and others like them who did good deeds and were not pleased with the worship of those who worshipped him? Ibn Jarir relied in his interpretation in the answer on the fact that what is for what does not have reason. Among the Arabs, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri converted to Islam after that, and he was one of the famous poets. He used to satirize the Muslims at first, then he said, apologizing: O Messenger of the King, my tongue is mended, it has not been torn since I was lost. If I follow Satan in his ways of error, and whoever deviates from his inclination will be doomed. And his saying: The greatest terror will not grieve them. It was said that what is meant by that is death. It was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Yahya ibn Rabi’ah on the authority of Ata’. It was also said that what is meant by the greatest terror is the blowing of the trumpet. This was said by al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Abu Sinan Sa’id ibn Sinan al-Shaibani, and Ibn Jarir chose it in his interpretation. It was also said: When the servant is ordered to the Fire. This was said by al-Hasan al-Basri. It was also said: When the Fire closes in on its people. This was said by Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Jurayj. It was also said: When death is slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire. This was said by Abu Bakr al-Hudhali in what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him. And his saying: And the angels will meet them, ‘This is your Day which you were promised.’ This means that the angels will say to them, giving them good tidings of the Day of their Return when they emerge from their graves, This is your Day which you were promised. That is, so hope for what pleases you.

Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. Narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah in his book Al-Ahadith Al-Mukhtara. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, Sufyan - meaning Al-Thawri - told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of his companions, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse was revealed: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will surely enter it, the polytheists said: So the angels, Ezra, and Jesus are worshipping besides God, so the verse was revealed: If these were gods, they would not have entered it, the gods that they worship, and all will abide therein eternally. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu Kudaynah, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he said: Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, may God have mercy on him, said in the Book of the Biography: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat one day with Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira in the mosque, then Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the mosque were more than one man from Quraysh, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke, and Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith came to him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to him until he silenced him, and he recited to him and them: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be brought to it. If these were gods, they would not have come to it. All will abide therein eternally. Therein they will have sighing, and therein they will not hear.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayri Al-Sahmi came and sat with them. Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira said to Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayri: By God, Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith did not stand up for Ibn Abdul Muttalib just now nor did he sit down, and Muhammad has claimed that I and what we worship of these gods of ours are fuel for Hell. Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayri said: By God, if I had found him, I would have argued with him. So ask Muhammad, everything that is worshipped besides God is in Hell with those who worship it, for we worship the angels. The Jews worship Ezra, and the Christians worship Christ Jesus, son of Mary. Al-Walid and those who were with him in the assembly were amazed at the words of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri, and they saw that he had argued and argued. So he mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “Whoever loves to be worshipped other than God is with those who worship Him. They only worship Satan and the one who commanded them to worship him.” And God revealed: “Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. They will not hear its hissing, and they will abide in that which their souls desire.” That is, Jesus and Ezra and those who worshipped from the rabbis and monks who continued in obedience to God, so those who worshipped them from the people of misguidance took them as lords other than God. And it was revealed regarding what they mentioned that they worshipped the angels and that they were the daughters of God: “And they said, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son. Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants.’” until His saying: “And whoever among them says, ‘I am a god other than Him,’ We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.” And it was revealed regarding what was mentioned regarding the matter of Jesus and that he is worshipped other than God. Al-Walid and those who were present with him were amazed. His argument and his argument: “And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, behold, your people turned away from him. And they said, ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’ They only cite him to you for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people. He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could have made from you angels on earth, succeeding [them].” And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour, so have no doubt about it. That is, the signs that were placed at his hands, such as reviving the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient evidence of knowledge of the Hour. He says: “So have no doubt about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.” And what Ibn al-Zubayri said is a great mistake, because the verse was revealed as an address to the people of Mecca regarding their worship of idols that are inanimate and do not have reason, so that it would be a rebuke and rebuke to their worshippers. For this reason, he said: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. So how can this be used against the Messiah, Ezra, and others like them who did good deeds and were not pleased with the worship of those who worshipped him? Ibn Jarir relied in his interpretation in the answer on the fact that what is for what does not have reason. Among the Arabs, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri converted to Islam after that, and he was one of the famous poets. He used to satirize the Muslims at first, then he said, apologizing: O Messenger of the King, my tongue is mended, it has not been torn since I was lost. If I follow Satan in his ways of error, and whoever deviates from his inclination will be doomed. And his saying: The greatest terror will not grieve them. It was said that what is meant by that is death. It was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Yahya ibn Rabi’ah on the authority of Ata’. It was also said that what is meant by the greatest terror is the blowing of the trumpet. This was said by al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Abu Sinan Sa’id ibn Sinan al-Shaibani, and Ibn Jarir chose it in his interpretation. It was also said: When the servant is ordered to the Fire. This was said by al-Hasan al-Basri. It was also said: When the Fire closes in on its people. This was said by Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Jurayj. It was also said: When death is slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire. This was said by Abu Bakr al-Hudhali in what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him. And his saying: And the angels will meet them, ‘This is your Day which you were promised.’ This means that the angels will say to them, giving them good tidings of the Day of their Return when they emerge from their graves, This is your Day which you were promised. That is, so hope for what pleases you.
21:104: God Almighty says: This will happen on the Day of Resurrection, On the Day when We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for books, as God Almighty said: “And they have not appraised God with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him.” Al-Bukhari said: Muqaddam bin Muhammad told us, my uncle Al-Qasim bin Yahya told me, on the authority of Ubaidullah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, God will seize the earths and the heavens will be in His right hand. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, narrated this only from this source. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Raqi told us, Muhammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Wasil, on the authority of Abu al-Malih al-Azdi, on the authority of Abu al-Jawza al-Azdi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God will fold the seven heavens and what is in them of creation, and the seven earths and what is in them of creation. He will fold all of that with His right hand, and all of that will be in His hands like a mustard seed. And His statement: Like the folding of a scroll for the books, it was said: What is meant by the scroll is the book, and it was said that what is meant by the scroll here is an angel from the angels. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn al-Ala’ told us, Yahya ibn Yaman told us, Abu al-Wafa al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, regarding the statement of God the Almighty: On the Day We will fold the heaven like the folding of a scroll for the books, he said: The scroll is an angel, and when he ascends with the supplication for forgiveness, he says: Write it down as light. And this is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Ibn Yaman with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn that the scroll King, and Al-Suddi said about this verse that the register is a king entrusted with the books, so when a person dies, his book is raised to the register, which folds it and raises it until the Day of Resurrection. It was said that what is meant by it is the name of a companion who used to write the revelation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Nasr ibn Ali Al-Jahdhami told us, Nuh ibn Qays told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On the Day We will fold up the heaven like the folding of a register for books, he said: The register is the man. Nuh said: And Yazid ibn Ka’b told me, he is Al-Awdhi, on the authority of Amr ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The register is a scribe for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And this is how Abu Dawud and Al-Nasa’i narrated it, both of them on the authority of Qutaybah ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Nuh ibn Qays, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ka’b, on the authority of Amr ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: The register is a scribe for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Nasr ibn Ali Al-Jahdhami, as mentioned above, and Ibn Adi narrated it from the narration of Yahya ibn Amr ibn Malik. Al-Nakri, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a scribe called al-Sijil, and this is what he said: On the Day We will roll up the heaven as a scroll is rolled up for books. He said: Just as the scroll is rolled up for books, so will the heaven be rolled up. Then he said: It is not preserved. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said in his history: Abu Bakr al-Barqani informed us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya’qub al-Hajjaji informed us, Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Karkhi informed us that Hamdan ibn Sa’id told them, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Numayr, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Umar, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: Al-Sijil was a scribe for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is very strange from the hadith of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, and it is not authentic at all. Likewise, what was mentioned above from Ibn Abbas, narrated by Abu Dawud and others, is also not authentic. A group of hadith masters have explicitly declared its fabrication, even though it is in Sunan Abu Dawud, among them our great Sheikh, the hadith master Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, may God prolong his life and extend his life, and conclude his life with righteous deeds. I have devoted a separate section to this hadith, praise be to God. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir stood up to deny this hadith, and he responded to it completely, and said: There is no one known among the companions whose name is As-Sajjil, and the scribes of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are known and there is no one among them whose name is As-Sajjil. He was right, may God have mercy on him, in that, and it is one of the strongest pieces of evidence for the strangeness of this hadith. As for the one who mentioned it among the names of the companions, he relied on this hadith and not on any other, and God knows best. The correct view from Ibn Abbas is that As-Sajjil is the document, as Ali bin Abi Talhah said, and Al-Awfi from him, and Mujahid, Qatadah and others stated that, and Ibn Jarir chose it because it is well-known in the language. Based on this, the meaning of the statement is that on the day when We fold the heaven like folding the scroll for the book, i.e. on the book in the sense of what is written, like His statement: So when they had submitted and laid it upon their foreheads, i.e. on the forehead, and it has similar linguistic parallels, and God knows best. And His statement: “As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. It is a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it,” means that this will inevitably happen on the day when God will return the creatures to a new creation as He began them, and He is able to return them. This is bound to happen because it is part of the promise of God, who does not fail or change, and He is able to do that. That is why He said: Indeed, We were to do it. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ and Ibn Ja’far al-Ma’ni narrated to us, they said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of al-Mughirah ibn al-Nu’man, on the authority of Sa’eed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and delivered a sermon among us, and he said: “You will be gathered before God, the Almighty, barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. Just as We began the first creation, We will repeat it. It is a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We were to do it.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Shu’bah. Al-Bukhari mentioned it in his book regarding this verse. Laith ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid from Aisha from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar to that. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Just as We began the first creation, We will repeat it, he said: Everything will perish as it was the first time.
21:105: The Almighty says, informing about what He has decreed and decided for His righteous servants of happiness in this world and the hereafter and inheriting the earth in this world and the hereafter, as He says: "Indeed, the earth belongs to God. He causes to inherit it whom He wills of His servants. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous." And He says: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. And He says: "God has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made those before them successors, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them." And the Almighty informs that this is written in the religious and predestined books and it will inevitably happen. For this reason, the Almighty says: And We have already written in the Psalms, after the Reminder. Al-A'mash said: I asked Sa'id bin Jubayr about the Almighty's saying: And We have already written in the Psalms, after the Reminder. He said: The Psalms are the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. Mujahid said: The Psalms are the Book. Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha'bi, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and more than one said: The Psalms are what was revealed to David, and the Reminder is the Torah. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Remembrance is the Qur’an. Saeed bin Jubair said: The Remembrance is in the heaven. Mujahid said: The Psalms are the books after the Remembrance, and the Remembrance is the Mother of the Book with God. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, chose this. Zaid bin Aslam also said: It is the first book. Ath-Thawri said: It is the Preserved Tablet. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: The Psalms are the books that were revealed to the prophets, and the Remembrance is the Mother of the Book in which things are written before that. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: God, the Most High, informed in the Torah and the Psalms and His foreknowledge before the creation of the heavens and the earth that He would inherit the earth for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and admit them to Paradise, and they are the righteous. Mujahid said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants. He said: The land of Paradise. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Sha’bi, Qatadah, As-Suddi, Abu Salih, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Ath-Thawri also said: We are the righteous. Abu Ad-Darda’ said: We are the righteous. Al-Suddi said: They are the believers. His statement: Indeed in this is a message for a people who worship, means that in this Qur’an that We revealed to Our servant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, there is a message: for benefit and sufficiency for a people who worship, and they are those who worshipped God in accordance with what He legislated, loved, and was pleased with, and who preferred obedience to God over obedience to Satan and the desires of their souls. And His statement: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds. God the Almighty informs us that God made Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, a mercy to the worlds, meaning He sent him as a mercy to all of them. Whoever accepts this mercy and is grateful for this blessing will be happy in this world and the hereafter, and whoever rejects it and denies it will lose in this world and the hereafter, as God the Almighty said: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction? Hell, which they will burn, and wretched is the resting place. And God the Almighty said in describing the Qur’an: “Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guide and a cure. But those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place.’” Muslim said in his Sahih: Ibn Abi Umar told us, Marwan Al-Fazari told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Kaysan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: It was said, O Messenger of God, invoke curses upon the polytheists. He said, I was not sent to curse, but rather I was sent as a mercy. Muslim alone transmitted it. In the other hadith, I am but a mercy sent forth. It was narrated by Abdullah bin Abi Uwanah and others on the authority of Wakee’ on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibrahim Al-Harbi said: Others have narrated it on the authority of Wakee’ but did not mention Abu Hurairah. Al-Bukhari said the same when he was asked about this hadith, and he said: It was narrated by Hafs bin Ghiyath as a mursal hadith. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir said: Malik bin Saeed Al-Khamis narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he cited it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Al-Muqri’ and Abu Ahmad Al-Hakim, both on the authority of Bakr bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Sufi. Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari told us on the authority of Abu Usamah on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am only a mercy sent down. Then he cited it on the authority of Al-Salt bin Masoud on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah on the authority of Misa’ar on the authority of Saeed bin Khalid, on the authority of a man on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God sent me as a mercy sent down. I was sent to raise up some people and lower others.” Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Nafi’ al-Tahhan told us, Ahmad ibn Salih told us: I found a book in Medina on the authority of Abdul Aziz al-Darawardi and Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdul Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Auf, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salih al-Tammar, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of his father, who said: Abu Jahl said when he came to Mecca on his way back from Hamza: O people of Quraysh, Muhammad has come down to Yathrib and sent his scouts, and he only wants to harm you, so beware of passing through his path or approaching him, for he is like a ferocious lion. He is angry with you because you banished him as monkeys banish from their nests. By God, he has magicians, and I have never seen him or any of his companions without seeing devils with them. You have known the enmity of the sons of Qaylah, meaning the Aws and Khazraj, for he is an enemy who sought help from an enemy. Mut’im ibn Adi said to him: O Abu al-Hakam, by God, I have never seen anyone more truthful in speech, nor more faithful in his promise than your brother whom you banished. And when… You did what you did, so be the most restrained from it. Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith said: Be as tough as you were before, for if the sons of Qaylah get hold of you, they will not respect any covenant or pact with you. If you obey me, you will force them to flee to the valley of Kinanah or you will expel Muhammad from among them, and he will be alone and banished. As for the sons of Qaylah, by God, they are the same as the people of Dahlak in humiliation, and I will suffice you against their punishment. He said: I will give a side of me that is rough, despite the closeness and distance Khazraj men are humiliated when it comes to joking after seriousness. When this reached the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), he said, "By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I will kill them, crucify them, and guide them even though they are reluctant. I am a mercy sent by God, and He will not take me until God makes His religion prevail. I have five names: I am Muhammad and Ahmad. I am al-Mahi, by whom God will wipe out disbelief. I am al-Hashir, by whose feet the people will be gathered. I am al-Aqib." Ahmad ibn Salih said, I hope that the hadith is authentic. Imam Ahmad said, "Mu'awiyah ibn Amr told us, Zaidah told us, Amr ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qurrah al-Kindi, who said, 'Hudhayfah was in al-Mada'in and he was mentioning things that the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) had said. Hudhayfah came to Salman, and Salman said, 'O Hudhayfah, the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) delivered a sermon and said, 'Any man from my nation whom I curse or whom I revile in my anger, I am only a man from the children of Adam, and I become angry as you become angry. God has sent me as a mercy to the worlds, so make it a prayer for him on the Day of Resurrection.'" Abu Dawood narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Yunus on the authority of Zaidah. If it is said: What mercy was given to those who disbelieved in Him? The answer is what Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir narrated: Ishaq ibn Shahin told us, Ishaq al-Azraq told us, on the authority of al-Mas`udi, on the authority of a man called Sa`id, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds, he said: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, mercy will be written for him in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger will be spared from what befell the nations of subsidence and stoning. And this is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of al-Mas`udi, on the authority of Abu Sa`d, who is Sa`id ibn al-Marzban al-Baqqal, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it in a similar manner, and God knows best. And Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Abdun ibn Ahmad, on the authority of `Isa ibn Yunus al-Ramli, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Suwayd, on the authority of al-Mas`udi, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds, he said: Whoever follows him will have mercy in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever does not follow him will be spared from what befell the rest of the nations of subsidence, transformation, and stoning.

Al-Bukhari said the same when he was asked about this hadith, and he said: It was narrated by Hafs bin Ghiyath as a mursal hadith. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir said: Malik bin Saeed Al-Khamis narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he cited it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Al-Muqri’ and Abu Ahmad Al-Hakim, both on the authority of Bakr bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Sufi. Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari told us on the authority of Abu Usamah on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am only a mercy sent down. Then he cited it on the authority of Al-Salt bin Masoud on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah on the authority of Misa’ar on the authority of Saeed bin Khalid, on the authority of a man on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God sent me as a mercy sent down. I was sent to raise up some people and lower others.” Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Nafi’ al-Tahhan told us, Ahmad ibn Salih told us: I found a book in Medina on the authority of Abdul Aziz al-Darawardi and Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdul Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Auf, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salih al-Tammar, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of his father, who said: Abu Jahl said when he came to Mecca on his way back from Hamza: O people of Quraysh, Muhammad has come down to Yathrib and sent his scouts, and he only wants to harm you, so beware of passing through his path or approaching him, for he is like a ferocious lion. He is angry with you because you banished him as monkeys banish from their nests. By God, he has magicians, and I have never seen him or any of his companions without seeing devils with them. You have known the enmity of the sons of Qaylah, meaning the Aws and Khazraj, for he is an enemy who sought help from an enemy. Mut’im ibn Adi said to him: O Abu al-Hakam, by God, I have never seen anyone more truthful in speech, nor more faithful in his promise than your brother whom you banished. And when… You did what you did, so be the most restrained from it. Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith said: Be as tough as you were before, for if the sons of Qaylah get hold of you, they will not respect any covenant or pact with you. If you obey me, you will force them to flee to the valley of Kinanah or you will expel Muhammad from among them, and he will be alone and banished. As for the sons of Qaylah, by God, they are the same as the people of Dahlak in humiliation, and I will suffice you against their punishment. He said: I will give a side of me that is rough, despite the closeness and distance Khazraj men are humiliated when it comes to joking after seriousness. When this reached the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), he said, "By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I will kill them, crucify them, and guide them even though they are reluctant. Imam Ahmad said, "Mu'awiyah ibn Amr told us, Zaidah told us, Amr ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qurrah al-Kindi, who said, 'Hudhayfah was in al-Mada'in and he was mentioning things that the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) had said. The answer is what Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir narrated: Ishaq ibn Shahin told us, Ishaq al-Azraq told us, on the authority of al-Mas`udi, on the authority of a man called Sa`id, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds, he said: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, mercy will be written for him in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger will be spared from what befell the nations of subsidence and stoning. 21:107: The Almighty says, informing about what He has decreed and decided for His righteous servants of happiness in this world and the hereafter and inheriting the earth in this world and the hereafter, as He says: "Indeed, the earth belongs to God. He causes to inherit it whom He wills of His servants. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous." And He says: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. And He says: "God has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made those before them successors, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them." And the Almighty informs that this is written in the religious and predestined books and it will inevitably happen. For this reason, the Almighty says: And We have already written in the Psalms, after the Reminder. Mujahid said: The Psalms are the books after the Remembrance, and the Remembrance is the Mother of the Book with God. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, chose this. Zaid bin Aslam also said: It is the first book. Ath-Thawri said: It is the Preserved Tablet. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: The Psalms are the books that were revealed to the prophets, and the Remembrance is the Mother of the Book in which things are written before that. 21:108: God Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, to say to the polytheists, “It has only been revealed to me that your god is one God. So will you submit to Him?” That is, will you follow that, submit, and obey Him? But if they turn away, that is, abandon what you have called them to, then say, ‘I have given you notice on equal terms.’ That is, I have informed you that I am at war with you just as you are at war with me, and I am innocent of you just as you are innocent of me, like His statement, “But if they deny you, then say, ‘To me is my work, and to you is your work. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do.’” And He said, But if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them on equal terms. That is, let your knowledge and their knowledge of the throwing back of covenants be on equal terms. And so it is here, But if they turn away, then say, ‘I have given you notice on equal terms.’ That is, I have informed you of my innocence of you and your innocence of me, because I know that. And His statement: And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far means it will inevitably happen, but I have no knowledge of its nearness or its farness. Indeed, He knows what is said aloud and He knows what you conceal means that God knows all of the unseen and knows what His servants reveal and what they conceal. He knows the outward and the inward, and He knows the secret and what is more hidden, and He knows what His servants do in their outward and inward affairs, and He will reward them for that, both the little and the great. And His statement: And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time means, and I do not know, perhaps this is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time. Ibn Jarir said: Perhaps delaying that from you is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a specified term. Awn narrated it from Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. He said, ‘My Lord, judge with truth’ means, judge between us and our people who deny the truth. Qatada said: The prophets, peace be upon them, used to say: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of judges. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to say that. And on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, witnessed a battle, he would say: My Lord, judge with truth. And His statement: And our Lord, the Most Gracious, is sought for help against that which you describe, meaning against what they say and fabricate of lies and various positions of denial and slander, and God is sought for help against you in that. The last interpretation of Surat Al-Anbiya, peace be upon them, and praise and thanks be to God.

Qatada said: The prophets, peace be upon them, used to say: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of judges. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to say that. And on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, witnessed a battle, he would say: My Lord, judge with truth. And His statement: And our Lord, the Most Gracious, is sought for help against that which you describe, meaning against what they say and fabricate of lies and various positions of denial and slander, and God is sought for help against you in that. The last interpretation of Surat Al-Anbiya, peace be upon them, and praise and thanks be to God.
